search.what: Filters the list below by network name, address range (CIDR) or interface name (wg0, wg1…).
search.who: Anyone looking for one network among many.
search.effect: Only changes what this page shows; nothing is saved or changed on the server.

name.what: The name of the new VPN network, shown in the network selector, the topology and the firewall rules.
name.who: Operators who keep separate networks for groups of devices (for example office, servers, staff).
name.effect: Must be unique. It cannot be renamed later: to change it, delete the network and create it again.

cidr.what: The private address range of the network, for example 10.20.0.0/24. The hub takes the first address; devices get the next free ones.
cidr.who: Needed for every network: it decides which addresses its devices use.
cidr.effect: It may not overlap another network (the server refuses it). It cannot be changed later. Creating the network also creates a new WireGuard interface (wg1, wg2…) on its own UDP port starting at 51820, which must be reachable from the internet.

clientDns.what: The DNS servers written into this network's device configs: up to 3 IPv4 addresses, comma separated.
clientDns.who: Networks whose devices should resolve names through a particular server, for example an internal DNS reachable over the VPN.
clientDns.effect: Empty: full-tunnel devices use 1.1.1.1 and split-tunnel devices keep their own DNS. With a value, every device of the network uses it. Only new or re-downloaded configs change; configs already on devices stay as they are until you send them again.
